title: Support Operations Analysis Report
executive_summary: Analysis of 220 support tickets reveals a total labor cost of $17,445.07 and a mean resolution time of 75.7 minutes. Team Beta carries the highest labor cost share. Email tickets reopen at a rate more than twice that of chat tickets, and a small high-cost, low-satisfaction segment warrants targeted intervention. Agent workload is moderately concentrated, with the busiest agent handling 7.3% of all tickets.

key_findings.statement: The dataset contains 220 tickets with a mean resolution time of 75.7 minutes and a total labor cost of $17,445.07.
Team Beta incurred the highest labor cost at $6,928.72, followed by Gamma at $5,911.44 and Alpha at $4,604.91. Beta accounts for the largest share of total labor spend.
Chat tickets had the longest mean resolution time at 82.2 minutes, followed by phone at 74.1 minutes and email at 71.7 minutes.
Email tickets reopen at 15.2%, compared to 6.8% for chat — an increase of 122.5% relative to the chat rate, indicating email tickets are substantially more likely to require reopening.
Nine tickets meet the high-cost (labor_cost ≥ $100) and low-satisfaction (score ≤ 2) criteria, and 11.1% of these were reopened — a segment meriting priority review.

Resolution time has a median of 65.0 minutes and a standard deviation of 51.3 minutes, indicating notable spread. Mean satisfaction (where recorded) is 4.14 out of 5, with 14 tickets missing a satisfaction score.
Tickets were handled by 18 distinct agents. The busiest single agent resolved 16 tickets, representing 7.3% of total volume — a moderate but watchable concentration.

limitations: Both the cleaning and analysis pipeline stages reported validation failures; results should be treated as provisional until the underlying data quality issues are investigated and resolved.
Fourteen tickets are missing satisfaction scores, which may bias the reported satisfaction mean if missingness is non-random.
The high-cost, low-satisfaction segment contains only 9 tickets, making percentage-based conclusions (e.g., reopen rate) statistically fragile.
Labor cost calculations depend on the accuracy of the agent roster join; any unmatched records dropped during cleaning could distort team-level totals.
Channel-level resolution times and reopen rates reflect ticket volume imbalances across channels and should be interpreted alongside ticket counts per channel.
conclusion: Support operations show acceptable overall satisfaction (mean 4.14) but elevated email reopen rates (+122% vs. chat) and a costly low-satisfaction segment demand attention. Team Beta's disproportionate labor cost and the wide resolution-time spread (std 51.3 min) suggest process inconsistency. Resolving the pipeline validation failures is the immediate priority before acting on these findings.
